_readme: Live pointer, read at page load. Edit on the server and refresh — no rebuild needed. There are only two sources: the roster behind rosterApiUrl for login, and the one spreadsheet in sheetId for everything a parent reads.
_rosterApiUrl: SOURCE 1 — login. /api/lookup is the Netlify function. Requires GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and ROSTER_CSV_URL — and ADMIN_EMAILS for staff — in the SERVER environment. It accepts nothing but a Google ID token: an email address posted to it is refused.
_sheetId: SOURCE 2 — everything else. Share link of the single spreadsheet holding the trip content. Needs 'Anyone with the link → Viewer'. Leave blank if you are using publishedId instead.
_publishedId: SOURCE 2, the private-document route. Paste the File → Share → Publish to web link (it contains /d/e/2PACX-…). The spreadsheet itself stays Restricted; only this read-only snapshot is public. Wins over sheetId. Tabs are addressed by gid here, not by name, so put each tab's gid in 'gids' — with none set, the first tab is served.
_csvBase: Local CSV files instead of Google, for development only. Blank in production.
_gids: Only needed if a tab has been renamed — a gid survives renames and wins over the tab name.
_driveApiKey: Optional. Turns a Drive FOLDER link inside a Documents row into one card per file. Not a content source on its own.
_adminEmails: Leave empty. Staff are configured via ADMIN_EMAILS in the server environment — this file is public, and there is no reason to publish which addresses unlock every grade. A listed address still has to arrive with a verified Google token for that address.
_tripPhotos: The school's own photograph of each grade's trip, shown on the Overview tab with the sheet's Header Text over it. Keyed by grade id. PREFERRED: paste the Drive share link of the photo (Share → Anyone with the link → Viewer, then Copy link) — the app turns it into Drive's thumbnail URL itself and Drive resizes it to the width each place renders, so the school's bandwidth bill stays off the site's host and nobody has to hand-build a URL. A local file in public/trip-photos/ or any other public image URL still works and is passed through untouched. A link that is NOT shared 'anyone with the link' returns a sign-in page instead of an image; the banner catches that and falls back to the grade colour, so a wrongly-shared photo looks like no photo rather than a broken one — open the link in a private window to check. A grade with no entry falls back to a CREDITED Wikipedia photograph of the destination (reinstated 2026-08-21 on the school's instruction, after a term in which only Grade 7 had a real photo). The original reason for having no fallback still stands and is handled by the credit: the caption says the picture is of the place and not of the trip, so a parent does not read it as their child standing in it. A photograph listed here ALWAYS wins over the lookup. Set autoDestinationPhoto to false to turn the fallback off entirely and go back to the plain grade colour. NOTE: anything listed here is served publicly and is NOT behind the parent login, so adding a photograph of students is a publishing decision, not a configuration one. The g7 entry was published on 2026-08-17 on the school's instruction, with parental consent confirmed as on file.
_tripPhotosPerTrip: A grade that runs several trips can key a photo PER TRIP as "<gradeId>.<destination-slug>" — lowercase, non-alphanumerics to hyphens: "g11.mokhamal", "g11.ambapani", "g11.kilad", "g11.kevdi". Falls back to the grade's own key, so a single entry still covers a single-trip grade. Keyed by DESTINATION, not by position: a "g11.0" would point at a different trip the moment a row is inserted above it. The same keys work in tripCardPhotos. These four campsites have no photograph available anywhere — Wikipedia has no article and the Commons/Openverse hits are other places entirely (an Ambapani in Jharkhand, a Leipzig memorial for "Kilad") — so their cards keep the grade colour until the school pastes its own photo here.
_tripCardPhotos: The photograph on the grade card in the picker, keyed by grade id. Optional: a grade with no entry here uses its tripPhotos image, and with neither it keeps the grade's colour and icon. It exists separately because the card is a wide 2.6:1 strip while the trip page's banner fills the window, so the same file rarely crops well in both. Served publicly and not behind the login, exactly like tripPhotos, and takes a Drive share link the same way — fetched at 1200px wide here against the banner's 1600px, because the card is only a 132px strip.
_slidePreviews: OVERRIDE ONLY — normally leave this EMPTY. Since 2026-08-24 the Safety, Do's and don'ts and Things to carry decks are framed live from the SHEET's own smart chip in those three columns: the app turns the chip's /presentation/d/<id>/edit link into /embed, so every grade shows the deck the school filed against it with nothing to paste here. A deck only needs 'Anyone with the link -> Viewer' for that; it does NOT need File > Share > Publish to web. Fill a key here only to point one grade at a DIFFERENT deck from the file in its sheet cell, and expect it to WIN over the sheet — a stale entry here silently shows an old deck after staff update the sheet, which is exactly why the g7.* and mlc.* entries below were removed on 2026-08-24 (g7.safety had also stopped resolving: its published URL answered 401, so Grade 7's Safety frame was broken while the sheet's own link worked). Keys are FLAT '<gradeId>.<section>' strings where section is safety, dodont or carry; do NOT nest them, because config merging walks one level and would stringify a nested object. Both /pub and /presentation/d/<id>/edit links are accepted and rewritten to /embed. CHECK ANY LINK YOU PASTE OPENS THE DECK ITS KEY NAMES: three pasted here were once one position rotated (2026-08-17), so Safety showed the do-and-donts deck. Open the URL and read its title.
_autoDestinationPhoto: false turns off the Wikipedia destination photo used when a grade has no entry in tripPhotos, leaving the banner as the plain grade colour. A school photograph always wins over it either way.
_googleClientId: OAuth 2.0 Web client id. REQUIRED — Google Sign-In is the only way into this app, so with this blank nobody can sign in and the login page says so. Set it and One Tap signs a returning parent in with no click. The SAME id must also be set as GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID in the server environment, which is where the token is actually verified; the two must match or every sign-in is refused.
